backlog.spec: Lower the logit softcap value (likely 15 or 30 in forward) to 15 and compare. If it is already 15, try 20.

backlog.spec: Scale the initialization std of the attention and MLP init weights by 0.7 (smaller init). This could speed up early training. Edit init_weights only.

backlog.spec: Reduce Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon from 5 to 4 if configurable, which saves compute for a negligible quality cost.

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape: factor = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*progress_in_warmdown)) scaled to FINAL_LR_FRAC. Keep the same WARMDOWN_RATIO.

backlog.spec: Remove any per-step .item() sync or loss logging done every step, and log only every 20 steps. This reduces host sync overhead and gives more steps in 300 s. Keep the smoothed loss only for printing.
backlog.title: Disable torch compile recompile overhead: fixed-shape eval-free loop

backlog.spec: Try DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 96 and TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 if tokens per micro-batch divides evenly, to reduce accumulation to a single micro-step per optimizer step. It falls back to 64 if OOM.

backlog.spec: Multiply the normalized q and k by a constant 1.2 (a sharper attention temperature) after the QK RMS norm. Keep it a single constant in the attention forward.

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSS" (last layer still forced long by existing code) and also multiply q and k by a constant 1.2 after the QK RMS norm. Both single runs beat the incumbent slightly; this tests whether the gains combine.

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 and keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 so each optimizer step needs half the accumulation micro-steps. In a 300 s budget this roughly doubles the optimizer step count. Keep the LR schedule unchanged. Use only this one change to the batch size.
backlog.title: Batch 2**18 with grad accumulation off

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown in the LR multiplier function with a cosine decay: over the warmdown portion use 0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)) where p is the warmdown progress from 0 to 1, going to FINAL_LR_FRAC. Leave the warmdown ratio at 0.5 and change nothing else.
backlog.title: Cosine-shaped warmdown to zero

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training loss only. Compute it from the float logits in the forward pass when targets are given and the model is training. backlog.title: Z-loss on logits

backlog.spec: Reduce the Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon from 5 to 3 to cut optimizer overhead and get more steps in 300 s. Use the same coefficients and drop the last two iterations only. This is a small, self-contained change to the Muon orthogonalization loop.
backlog.title: Muon NS steps 3 for speed

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH=6 and ASPECT_RATIO=96, so the width is 576 rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM (640 if the code rounds up). The model is shallower and wider, with faster steps and more tokens seen in 300 s. Change nothing else. Check that the model_dim is divisible by HEAD_DIM 128.
backlog.title: Depth 6 with ASPECT_RATIO 96

backlog.spec: Train the first 30% of the time budget on sequences truncated to half length (for example, use only the first half of each sequence for the loss and input, with the batch tokens count kept the same by doubling the rows), then use full length. If this is awkward, simply cut the inputs and targets to half length during the first 30% of progress. This gives faster early steps. Keep evaluation unchanged.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA of the model parameters with decay 0.999 updated every step after 50% of training progress. Copy the EMA weights into the model just before the final evaluation. Do not touch the evaluation call itself. Memory cost is one extra copy of the parameters.
backlog.title: Weight averaging (EMA) of the final model

backlog.spec: If the model uses value embeddings with a gate, multiply the value-embedding contribution by 2 (for example, 2*sigmoid(gate)) so its initial effect is stronger, leaving everything else unchanged. If there is no gate, add a learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 1.5 on the value embedding contribution.
backlog.title: Untie value-embedding gate init and scale to 2

backlog.spec: During training only, replace 5% of the input token ids at random with a fixed token id 0 before the embedding lookup. Targets stay the same. This is a light regularizer. Turn it off in the last 20% of progress. Do not touch the evaluation path.
backlog.title: Dropout-free token masking regularizer

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 so grad accumulation drops to 2 steps (DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE stays 64). Halving the batch was the biggest win so far, so this continues the trend of more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Batch 2**17 with device batch 64

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**16 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 32 so there is exactly one micro-step per optimizer step (32 seqs x 2048 tokens, if sequence length is 2048; otherwise choose DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE*MAX_SEQ_LEN equals 2**16). Also scale MATRIX_LR by 0.8 to compensate for the noisier gradients. This tests the extreme of the small-batch, many-steps regime.
backlog.title: Batch 2**16 no accumulation, bold

backlog.spec: Use a smaller effective batch early in training and grow it later. For the first 30% of the time budget use grad accumulation of 1 micro-step (about 2**16 tokens), then 2 micro-steps, then 4 micro-steps for the last 30% (the 2**18 level). Compute the number of accumulation steps from training progress each step, and divide the loss by the current accumulation count. Keep the LR schedule unchanged.
backlog.title: Linear batch-size ramp

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated every step with torch._foreach_lerp_ under no_grad. Just before the final evaluation, swap the EMA weights into the model. Do not touch the evaluation call itself. If the EMA hurts under warmdown-to-zero it will show up as a loss, but averaging may help with the small batch.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.75 and change the warmdown decay from linear to cosine: lr multiplier = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1-FINAL_LR_FRAC)*0.5*(1+cos(pi*(1-cooldown_fraction))), where cooldown_fraction is the remaining fraction of the warmdown phase. Both changes together form one schedule experiment.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.75 with cosine shape

backlog.spec: Lower the Muon momentum target from its current final value (probably 0.95) to 0.9, and shorten the momentum warmup accordingly. With smaller batches and more steps, less momentum may track the loss surface better. Change only the momentum schedule values.
backlog.title: Muon momentum 0.9 plateau

backlog.spec: Reduce the logit softcap (the tanh softcap applied to the lm_head output, currently probably 30) to 15. Keep the formula cap*tanh(logits/cap). Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 15

backlog.spec: Change the MLP hidden dimension from 4*n_embd to 3*n_embd and set DEPTH = 10 with ASPECT_RATIO adjusted to 51 so model_dim stays near 512 (round to a multiple of HEAD_DIM). This trades width per layer for more layers at a similar parameter count and per-step cost. Verify that the model still fits memory at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64.
backlog.title: MLP expansion 3x with depth 10

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits.float(), dim=-1)**2) to the training loss only, not to the evaluation path. Implement it in the training loop or in the forward pass when targets are given and the model is in training mode, without changing the evaluation call. It stabilizes the logit scale.
backlog.title: Z-loss on logits

backlog.spec: Train the first 25% of the time budget on sequences cropped to 512 tokens (reshape each batch so tokens per step stay constant, i.e. 4x more sequences of length 512), then switch to the full length. Use a separate set of window sizes per phase if the sliding window requires it. Cheaper attention early gives more steps. Accept one recompile at the switch (mark it as outside the timed budget if the harness allows, otherwise keep it to one switch).
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum 512 to full

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation falls to 2 given seq len 2048). The 2**19 to 2**18 change gave the largest gain so far, and more optimizer steps in 300 s may help again. If the code scales LRs by batch, leave that as is.
backlog.title: Batch 2**17 with 2 accumulation steps

backlog.spec: Keep an exponential moving average of the model parameters (decay 0.999, updated every optimizer step with torch._foreach_lerp_ on a copy in bf16/fp32). Before the final evaluation call, swap the EMA weights into the model. Do not change the evaluation call itself. If the harness evaluates the model object, copy EMA weights into the model's parameters in place after training ends. Start the EMA only after the LR warmdown begins (progress>0.5) so it does not average early bad weights.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: Change the logit softcap applied to the final logits (the value like 15 * tanh(logits/15)) to 15 if it differs, or add one if absent: logits = 15*torch.tanh(logits/15), computed in float32. Apply it in both training and eval forward paths, as the code already does, so there is no train/eval mismatch.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 15

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008. Only this constant changes. The lm_head is trained with Adam, and in a short budget it may be underfit.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 and make the MLP hidden size 3*n_embd rather than 4*n_embd in the MLP class (c_fc out and c_proj in). Keep ASPECT_RATIO 64 so the model dimension rounds to 640 and has 5 heads of dim 128. Parameter count stays about the same, but depth is higher. If the dimension rounding needs it, ensure the dimension is a multiple of HEAD_DIM.
backlog.title: MLP hidden ratio 3x with depth 10

backlog.spec: Do not change the data pipeline. Instead, for the first 30% of training time, truncate each training batch to the first 512 tokens of every sequence (x[:, :512], y[:, :512]) and run extra micro-steps so tokens per step stay constant. If that is awkward, keep the micro-batch count and accept fewer tokens per step. Use full length afterwards. Short sequences are cheaper, so early steps run faster. This may trigger a torch.compile recompile, so mark the shape dynamic or accept one recompile at the switch, which is not counted in the budget.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 and WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 together. A longer decay with a nonzero floor keeps learning going to the end of the 300 s run.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05 with warmdown 0.7

backlog.spec: Initialize attention c_proj and MLP c_proj weights to zero in init_weights, if they are not already zero. This makes every block start as an identity. Do not change any other init. If they are already zero, instead scale the init of the c_v/value path to std 0.5 of the current one.
backlog.title: Zero-init residual output projections

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.8, 0.99). A longer second-moment window gives steadier updates for embedding and scalar parameters at batch 2**18. Only the constant changes.

memo: Incumbent is slot 6 (1.0981). Halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 gave -0.0165, the only accepted change and by far the largest gain. More optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s budget is the lever that works. Hurt: HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0133), DEPTH=6 (+0.0059), EMBEDDING_LR 0.4 (+0.0055), Adam beta1 0.9 (+0.0035), z-loss (+0.0031). Neutral: weight decay 0.1 (+0.0000) and 0.0 (-0.0002). Small possible gains, all single runs and so maybe noise, each measured vs the incumbent: SSSS plus q/k scale 1.2 (-0.0048), WARMUP_RATIO 0.02 (-0.0039), MATRIX_LR 0.05 (-0.0036), ns_steps=3 (-0.0025), logging every 20 steps (-0.0016). Next: 1) Try TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17. 2) Stack the small gains (SSSS with q/k scale, warmup, MATRIX_LR 0.05, ns_steps=3, less logging) on the new batch size, since they may add up. 3) Replicate any gain under 0.005 before accepting. Avoid head-count, depth and regularization changes.
